dir: Use the official California registration information when checking which janitorial requirements apply to a provider.
dirfaq: This reference explains the state registration program. It does not verify a particular company’s staffing, screening or access policies.
cdc: CDC guidance for cleaning a facility
Consult this guidance for the distinction between cleaning and disinfection and for considering a facility’s surfaces and use.
hazcom: This is a primary reference for workplace chemical information, labeling and relevant worker training requirements.
chemical: OSHA guidance for workers using cleaning chemicals
Use this worker safety resource when discussing chemical handling and suitable precautions, rather than assuming every cleaning product is harmless.
safer: Check an exact product in the official list instead of assuming an environmental marketing claim establishes certification.
saferfaq: This reference explains the program and supports informed questions about certified products and their intended use.
walk: This reference addresses workplace walking surface conditions. It is relevant when cleaning affects access or creates a temporarily restricted area.
mold: EPA guidance on mold and moisture
Use this resource for understanding why a moisture problem can require attention beyond removing a visible surface mark.
moldcontrol: This resource identifies moisture control as central to mold control. Exterior washing should not be confused with resolving every building moisture problem.
foodguide: Los Angeles County retail food inspection guide
Restaurant operators can use the local guide to understand inspection concerns and distinguish cleaning work from their wider operating responsibilities.
foodinspect: Los Angeles County restaurant inspection information
Consult the local inspection information rather than relying on a cleaning provider’s promise of a particular inspection result.
cri: Carpet and Rug Institute cleaning standards
Review the applicable carpet maintenance standard alongside the carpet manufacturer’s care information and the property’s use.
criguide: This industry resource provides context for a commercial carpet maintenance program. It does not establish one interval suitable for every property.
hardie: This manufacturer guidance illustrates why an exterior material’s own care instructions matter when choosing a cleaning approach.
hardiefaq: Consult the manufacturer information for its products. Do not apply a recommendation for one material automatically to other building surfaces.
storm: City of Los Angeles pollutant discharge requirements
Use the local requirements when reviewing wash water responsibilities. The service plan should reflect the actual site and applicable rules.
windowrules: This primary safety reference concerns window cleaning operations. Glass coatings and finishes also need their own manufacturer care information.
windowladder: Review the relevant access requirements with a qualified provider rather than assuming every window can be reached using the same equipment.
